title: a-second-agent-owns-a-corpus-through-the-one-tree-tool
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the_hermes_corpus_keeps_growing) -> PROVED
intention: hermes deposits its learnings into Cairn's existing graph trees under owner='hermes' rather than keeping a private lexical-overlap graph, so a second agent's learning lives in the store, behind the one gate, readable by CC and by Akien without attaching to a running process.
why: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — running a weaker duplicate of a graph already built here is re-deriving a settled answer); Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner, except a tool, which has users — this is that clause used for the first time by a caller who is not CC); Law 10 (a second agent's learning must be measurable, and learning in ~/.hermes is not).
how: nexus_table(nexus, owner='hermes'). Its learnings ride the existing deposit_learning / counsel / propose verbs; its vectors come from nomic-embed-text through inference_domain like every other embed in the system. There is no new machinery to write — `owner` is already a call parameter on every verb, which is the whole point.
falsifier: DONE when a hermes-authored learning is retrievable by counsel under owner='hermes', and CC can read it without attaching to hermes' process. WRONG INTENT if hermes' skill and memory objects cannot be expressed as (content, vector, provenance) without distorting them — in which case the honest answer is two stores that AGREE and say so, never one store that flattens the other's shape and calls it integration.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — running a weaker duplicate of a graph already built here is re-deriving a settled answer); Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner, except a tool, which has users — this is that clause used for the first time by a caller who is not CC); Law 10 (a second agent's learning must be measurable, and learning in ~/.hermes is not).

watchme.trigger: each deposit_learning call landing under owner='hermes'
watchme.enough: when the corpus has taken deposits across 5 separate hermes sessions — a corpus that takes one deposit and then stops is the dead-store failure this watch exists to catch, and 5 sessions is enough to tell a live one from a launch artifact
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: a hermes-authored learning retrievable by counsel under owner='hermes', plus the deposit count over time
watchme.nexus: the hermes-owned corpus itself — the watch reads the thing it watches, which is the cheapest possible instrument here
watchme.consumer: CC, who is the other reader of that corpus and the first to notice if it goes stale

gates_bound: proof gate — proofs beside the code, run by the tester under netns isolation; teeth a hollow build could not pass (Law 8).
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage, never to a paragraph (Law 3 + the deterministic-red rule: fixed, or carrying a ruling from Akien).
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.

emit chokepoint — every crossing rides cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit at the component's own address carrying this ticket id; BUILDME refused without a berthed validate packet claiming it, PROVED refused without a complete passing verdict artifact.
owner: CC builds the mapping; the hermes device owns the corpus it deposits into (owner='hermes'); cairn/tools/tree is a TOOL and has users, not an owner
depends_on: QUEUED ON the hermes device ticket (cb97524c0e8e) (sibling, same idea). There is no corpus to own until there is a hermes.

cast_checks.assumption_check: The load-bearing assumption is that hermes' skill and memory objects map onto (content, vector, provenance) without loss. Measured: its skills are SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter (name, description, version, author, license, platforms, prerequisites, metadata) and its memories are MEMORY.md / USER.md chunks — both LOOK like content with provenance. Not measured: whether the frontmatter carries anything that is neither content nor provenance and would be dropped silently. The falsifier is written so a loss routes to two honest stores rather than to a quiet flattening.
cast_checks.missing_check: Yes, one: WHICH NEXUS. The intent says owner='hermes' and never says what nexus name its learnings deposit under. tree.py's verbs take both, and the existing nexi (orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate) are the chart's. My read, not ratified: hermes gets its own nexus names rather than depositing into the chart's, because a chart nexus is the memory of how CHART STAGES decide, and a second agent's learnings are not that. Recorded so the builder does not quietly pick one.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: Stands and is cheap to check: a hermes-authored learning retrievable by counsel under owner='hermes', readable by CC without attaching to hermes' process. HORIZON: the first hermes learning deposit. Wrong-intent tell is written and is the important half — if the mapping distorts hermes' shape, the honest answer is TWO stores that agree and say so, never one store that flattens the other and calls it integration.
cast_checks.collision_check: Checked whether Law 6 permits a non-CC owner of a corpus: it does, and cleanly — ownership gates writes to STATE, hermes would gate its own, and tree.py holds no state of its own to gate. That is the Law's own test being PASSED, not an exception carved. No collision found. A distinction worth recording: this is the first time the tools rung's owner-as-call-parameter design serves an owner that is not CC, which is a claim tree.py's charter makes and nothing has yet tested.
cast_checks.builder_check: (1) THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING TO BUILD and a builder should be told so explicitly, because the reflex on a ticket like this is to write a wrapper. nexus_table, deposit_learning, counsel and propose all already take owner. (2) VECTORS ARE THE CALLER'S: tree.py's own note says vectors arrive as DATA and the embed call goes out through inference_domain. So the work is the MAPPING from a hermes skill/memory to (content, vector, provenance), and nothing else. (3) THE REAL RISK is scope: do not build a sync daemon, do not mirror ~/.hermes, do not poll. A deposit happens when hermes learns, event-driven, or it does not happen. (4) DEPENDS on the hermes device ticket for there to be a hermes at all — this reads queued on it.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Let it keep ~/.hermes and mirror the contents into the trees — rejected, and by a precedent from this very system: inference_domain deliberately CUT spend from its trail rather than carry it in two places, because one number in two records is a number that can drift. Two records of one learning is the same defect with a longer fuse.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: cairn/tools/tree/tree.py, whose charter states outright that `owner` is a CALL PARAMETER, that the tool holds no corpus and addresses whichever corpus its caller owns, and that this IS the proof of what 'a tool has users, not an owner' means in code (Akien, 2026-08-13). This intent is that design meeting its first non-CC caller — prior art so exact that the intent is mostly an act of USING it.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That hermes' skill and memory objects map onto (content, vector, provenance) without loss. Unverified — measured only that its skills are SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter and its memories are MEMORY.md / USER.md chunks, both of which LOOK like content with provenance. Whether the mapping is lossless is the first thing to test, and the falsifier is written so that a loss routes to two honest stores rather than to a quiet flattening.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: None. The nearest question is whether Law 6 even permits hermes to own a corpus: it does, and cleanly — ownership gates writes to STATE, hermes would gate its own, and tree.py has no state of its own to gate. That is the Law's own test being passed, not an exception being carved.
